title: PRD: Runtime Fidelity Negotiator & Onboarding Simulation Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This document defines the Product Requirement and rollout playbook for the Runtime Fidelity Negotiator (RFN): a service and simulation harness that (1) negotiates an appropriate response fidelity (quality/compute tradeoff) per-session or per-route based on customer SLA, latency and cost constraints, and (2) provides a self-serve onboarding simulator that lets customers preview cost/latency tradeoffs against representative traffic before committing to capacity or fidelity tiers.

Background and motivation:
- Customers routinely request predictable latency and cost guarantees while also requiring output quality suitable for their UX. Current options require manual rule authoring or coarse-grained fidelity tiers that are hard to validate before deployment.
- The RFN will reduce friction for hosted-to-dedicated/on-prem migrations by giving an automated negotiation layer and an experimental sandbox for customers to simulate their workloads against fidelity policies and pricing implications.

Goals (what success looks like):
1) Provide an API and runtime that returns a fidelity decision within 30ms median for <= 99th%-tile client negotiation latency <= 150ms under 95th percentile load.
2) Onboarding simulator that accurately predicts token-level cost within ±10% compared to production over a representative 24h synthetic replay.
3) Policy primitives that support: per-route SLOs, per-tenant budget caps, adaptive fallback chains and quantization-aware candidate scoring.

Non-goals:
- RFN is not a full billing engine. It surfaces crediting recommendations and signals to billing, but accounting remains in billing service.
- RFN does not replace model evaluation; it relies on model onboarding quality metadata provided by Applied ML.

Personas:
- Platform engineers: want contract-level guarantees and diagnostics during migration.
- Customer SREs: validate that production fidelity choices meet latency/cost targets.
- Product managers & Solutions engineers: design fidelity defaults for product lines.

Success metrics (first 6 months):
- 50 enterprise onboarding simulations completed with error <=10% vs. observed cost.
- 80% of negotiation calls return decision in <=30ms median.
- 30% reduction in initial overprovisioning when customers adopt RFN simulator vs. previous baseline.

Functional requirements:
1) Public negotiation API: POST /v1/fidelity/negotiate
   - Input: route_id, tenant_id, request_profile (tokens_estimate, response_max_tokens), latency_target_ms, cost_budget_usd_per_1k_tokens (optional), sample_prompts (optional, list hash ids)
   - Output: fidelity_decision {variant_id, quantization_profile, expected_latency_ms, expected_cost_per_1k_tokens, confidence_score}
   - Example payload:
```
{
  "route_id":"checkout-chat",
  "tenant_id":"tenant-42",
  "request_profile": {"avg_input_tokens":120, "max_output_tokens":350},
  "latency_target_ms":150,
  "cost_budget_usd_per_1k_tokens":0.12
}
```
   - Negotiation must be idempotent and log a decision event for audit.

2) Policy language v1 (declarative):
   - Allow constraints: latency:<ms>, cost:<usd/1k>, min_quality:<metric:threshold>, allowed_variants:[ids], blacklist_variants:[ids], fallback_chain:ordered list.
   - Must support tenant-level overrides and route-level defaults.

3) Simulator CLI and UI component:
   - CLI: rfnsim run --tenant tenant-42 --profile profile.yaml --duration 24h --out results.json
   - UI: one-click scenario creation from sample prompt sets, output cost/latency histograms and per-variant confusion metrics.

Non-functional requirements:
- Negotiator availability: 99.9% overall, regionally redundant.
- Negotiation latency: median <=30ms, p99 <=150ms under standard load (500 rps regionally).
- Throughput: baseline capacity 1k negotiation QPS per region, autoscaling to 5k QPS.
- Security: requests authenticated with route token, negotiation decisions stored in audit log with tenant-scoped encryption.

Simulation harness and benchmark scenarios:
- Scenario A (Transactional baseline): 95% short requests (avg input 30 tokens, response 50 tokens).
- Scenario B (Conversational long-tail): 60% mid-size (120 input, 300 output), 40% long (500+ tokens).
- Scenario C (Bursty enterprise): diurnal + sudden 10x bursts lasting 2m every 6h.

For each scenario simulator must produce:
- Per-variant latency profile (p50/p95/p99),
- Token-cost projection (USD/1k tokens),
- Fidelity-impact on quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim depending on route),
- Regression delta vs. model baseline.

Pricing & packaging implications (summary table in text):
- Fidelity tier mapping:
  - high-fidelity: 1.0x base cost, recommended for 'must-pass' routes.
  - balanced: 0.65x base cost, default for interactive consumer routes.
  - economy: 0.4x base cost, suitable for low-sensitivity batch tasks.
- Suggested crediting guidance: when RFN selects a lower-fidelity variant as fallback, bill at fallback multiplier but surface an "fidelity credit" of (1 - multiplier) that can be used for migration credits if customer upgrades to a higher SLA within 30 days.

Rollout plan (phases):
1) Internal alpha (4 weeks): runtime prototype + simulator runs against internal traffic. Metrics: negotiation latency, simulator accuracy vs. replay. Owners: Runtime (Marcus Chen), Applied ML (Sofia Martinez).
2) Partner beta (8–12 weeks): 3 pilot customers, dedicated SRE runbooks, billing hook for fidelity credits, explicit opt-in. Collect per-tenant simulation vs. production deltas.
3) GA: public API, console integration, packaged as part of Dedicated onboarding toolkit.

Observability & telemetry (events and dashboards):
- Decision events: fidelity_decision.created (fields: tenant_id, route_id, decision_id, variant_id, expected_cost, expected_latency)
- Simulator events: sim.run.started, sim.run.completed, sim.estimate.delta (estimate vs observed)
- Dashboards: per-tenant fidelity mix, cost-savings estimate, simulator accuracy over time. Alerts: simulator_accuracy_drop (>=15% deviation for 3 successive sims), negotiation_latency_slo_breach (>150ms p99).

Compatibility and fallback behavior:
- If RFN is unavailable, runtime must apply the route default fidelity_decision with a warning metric (runtime.fidelity.fallback_applied).
- RFN decisions are tagged with compatibility flags (requires-kv-cache, supports-quant128, needs-atten-optim) to ensure candidate model variants are compatible with runtime path.

Sample CLI & API examples:
- Negotiation call (curl):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/fidelity/negotiate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ROUTE_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"route_id":"checkout-chat","tenant_id":"tenant-42","request_profile":{"avg_input_tokens":120,"max_output_tokens":350},"latency_target_ms":150}'
```
- Simulation run example (CLI):
```
rfnsim run --tenant tenant-42 --scenario conversational-longtail --duration 24h --out report.json
```

Operational runbooks (high level):
1) Investigate negotiation latency spike:
   - Check negotiator cluster CPU/GPU (if applicable) and queue depth.
   - Verify policy store (consul/kvs) latency for policy fetch.
   - If p99 >250ms, toggle emergency static default route and scale negotiator ASG + alert SRE.
2) Simulator accuracy drop:
   - Run replay with raw production traces, compare token-count distribution.
   - Validate model variant performance drift flagged by Applied ML.

Ownership, milestones and open decisions:
- Product owner: Aisha Patel. Engineering leads: Marcus Chen (Runtime), Sofia Martinez (Applied ML).
- Milestones:
  - Prototype complete: 2026-09-15 (done)
  - Internal alpha: 2026-10-10
  - Partner beta start: 2026-11-01
  - GA: 2027-01-15
- Open decisions:
  - Final pricing multiplier thresholds for the fidelity credit program (Finance + Go-to-market).
  - Whether simulator will run deterministic sketches or full-token generation sampling by default.

Appendix: small YAML policy example:
```
policy:
  route: checkout-chat
  constraints:
    latency_ms: 150
    max_cost_usd_per_1k: 0.12
    min_quality: {embedding_sim: 0.86}
  fallbacks:
    - variant: rwd-13b-quant
      multiplier: 0.65
    - variant: rwd-7b-quant-ev
      multiplier: 0.4
```

End of document. For implementation tasks see the linked design tickets and runtime runbook.
